subproblems.title: The tangent space of an embedded submanifold is the range of the derivative of any local representation
subproblems.statement: Let ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be a local representation of N ⊆ ℝ^P in the sense of Simon Ch. 2 §4 (4.1): V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ of class C^r on V with r ≥ 1, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. Then for every v ∈ V the tangent space T_{ψ(v)}N = {γ'(0) : γ ∈ C¹((−1,1); ℝ^P), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = ψ(v)} (tangentSpace N (ψ v)) equals the range of Dψ(v).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → v ∈ V → tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2 §4 (definition of T_yM for an embedded submanifold, and its identification with Dψ(ℝ^d)); this is the identification T_{ψ_y(v)} = range Dψ_y(v) of step 2 of the supplied proof of the selected node, used for (7.1) through the sibling chart_jacobian.
1. Setup. Put y := ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ N and L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v; since V is open and r ≥ 1, ψ is differentiable at v with derivative L. L is injective, so (finite dimension) there is c > 0 with |Lh| ≥ c|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^d; range L is a linear subspace, hence closed.
2. range L ⊆ T_yN. Let w = La. If a = 0, the constant curve γ ≡ y works (y ∈ N). Otherwise choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(v, ρ) ⊆ V and κ > 0 with κ|a| < ρ, and let σ(s) := κ·tanh(s/κ), a smooth function with σ(0) = 0, σ'(0) = 1 and |σ(s)| < κ. Put γ(s) := ψ(v + σ(s)a). Then v + σ(s)a ∈ V for all s, so γ is C^r (in particular C¹) on ℝ ⊇ (−1,1), γ(ℝ) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = y, and γ'(0) = Dψ(v)(σ'(0)a) = La = w. Hence w ∈ T_yN.
3. Embedding property. If z_k ∈ V and ψ(z_k) → y then z_k → v: the set K := {ψ(z_k) : k} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact and contains every z_k; any cluster point z ∈ V of (z_k) satisfies ψ(z) = y = ψ(v) by continuity, so z = v by injectivity on V; hence z_k → v.
4. T_yN ⊆ range L. Let w ∈ T_yN, witnessed by γ. As γ is continuous at 0 and W is open, there is s_0 ∈ (0,1) with γ(s) ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V) for |s| < s_0; write γ(s) = ψ(β(s)) with β(s) ∈ V (unique by injectivity). By step 3 (applied along sequences s_k → 0), β(s) → v as s → 0.
5. Write ψ(z) − y = L(z − v) + ρ(z) with |ρ(z)| ≤ η(|z − v|)·|z − v|, η(t) → 0 as t → 0. For |s| small, η(|β(s) − v|) ≤ c/2, hence |γ(s) − y| ≥ c|β(s) − v| − (c/2)|β(s) − v|, i.e. |β(s) − v| ≤ (2/c)|γ(s) − y|. Since γ is differentiable at 0, |γ(s) − y| ≤ C|s| for small |s|; thus |β(s) − v| = O(|s|) and |ρ(β(s))| = o(|s|).
6. Hence (γ(s) − y)/s = L((β(s) − v)/s) + o(1), so the difference quotients lie within o(1) of range L. Letting s → 0, w = γ'(0) belongs to the closure of range L, which is range L. Together with step 2, tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v).
(Reused accepted declaration; its frozen type is byte-identical to the accepted node's.)
proof_key_steps: Curves s ↦ ψ(v + σ(s)a) with σ smooth, bounded, σ'(0) = 1 show range Dψ(v) ⊆ T_{ψ(v)}N.
Properness and injectivity make ψ^{-1} continuous at ψ(v) along N ∩ W.
Injectivity of Dψ(v) gives |β(s) − v| = O(|γ(s) − ψ(v)|), so difference quotients of any curve in N lie in range Dψ(v) up to o(1).

subproblems.title: Injective area formula with the Gram-determinant Jacobian, and Borel measurability of that Jacobian (Simon Ch. 2, (3.1)–(3.5)); reused accepted declaration
subproblems.statement: Let m, P ∈ ℕ and f : ℝ^m → ℝ^P. Let Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x (the zero map where f is not differentiable), e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1, and Jf(x) := (det[⟨Df(x)e_k, Df(x)e_l⟩]_{k,l})^{1/2} (Real.sqrt). Then (i) Jf : ℝ^m → ℝ is Borel measurable; (ii) for every Borel s ⊆ ℝ^m such that f is differentiable at every x ∈ s with Df(x) injective and f is injective on s, and for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (no measurability required), ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_s ofReal(Jf(x)) · g(f(x)) dλ(x), where H^m := μHE[m] on ℝ^P and λ := volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m P : ℕ) (f : Euclid m → Euclid P), Measurable (fun x => Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single l 1))))) ∧ ∀ s : Set (Euclid m), MeasurableSet s → (∀ x ∈ s, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) → (∀ x ∈ s, Injective (fderiv ℝ f x)) → InjOn f s → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ y in f '' s, g y ∂μHE[m] = ∫⁻ x in s, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single l 1))))) * g (f x) ∂volume
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, §3, (3.1)–(3.5): the area formula for an injective map with injective derivative, with Simon's Jacobian Jf = (det((Df)ᵀDf))^{1/2} of (3.3) written as a Gram determinant. This is the theorem that step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected node cites as SimonGMT injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative, together with the weighted form that its step 6 derives from it. That SimonGMT theorem and Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet lie outside Submission's import closure, so the accepted declaration inlines the SimonGMT/Mathlib argument under the frozen imports; the steps below follow it. Notation: J_f denotes the Jacobian Jf of the statement; for a linear L : ℝ^m → ℝ^P put G(L) := √det[⟨Le_k, Le_l⟩]_{k,l<m}, so J_f = G∘Df. H^m := μHE[m]; L^m := λ = volume on ℝ^m.

1. (G is continuous.) Each entry L ↦ ⟨Le_k, Le_l⟩ is continuous on the finite-dimensional space of linear maps ℝ^m → ℝ^P, the determinant is a polynomial in the entries, and the square root is continuous. Hence G is continuous.

2. (Proof of (i).) The map x ↦ Df(x) ∈ L(ℝ^m, ℝ^P) is Borel measurable for every f (Mathlib measurable_fderiv). Hence J_f = G∘Df is Borel measurable.

3. (Linear area formula.) Let L be injective. Then G(L) > 0 and H^m(L(S)) = G(L)·L^m(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^m. Indeed, range L has dimension m (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj). Let φ be the linear isometry from range L onto ℝ^m that sends an orthonormal basis of range L (indexed by Fin m) to the standard basis, and put B := φ∘L : ℝ^m → ℝ^m. Then L = ι∘B, where ι := (inclusion of range L)∘φ⁻¹ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P is a linear isometry. B is injective, hence invertible, so det B ≠ 0. As ι preserves inner products, ⟨Le_k, Le_l⟩ = ⟨Be_k, Be_l⟩ = (MᵀM)_{kl}, where M is the standard matrix of B; hence det[⟨Le_k, Le_l⟩] = (det B)² and G(L) = |det B| > 0. Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries, so H^m(L(S)) = H^m(ι(B(S))) = H^m(B(S)); on Euclidean ℝ^m, H^m = L^m (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); and L^m(B(S)) = |det B|·L^m(S) for every S (Measure.addHaar_image_linearMap). Hence H^m(L(S)) = G(L)·L^m(S).

4. (Distance comparison.) Let S ⊆ ℝ^m, K ≥ 0, and φ, ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P with ψ injective on S and |φ(x) − φ(y)| ≤ K|ψ(x) − ψ(y)| for all x, y ∈ S. Then h := φ∘(ψ|_S)⁻¹ is K-Lipschitz on ψ(S) and h(ψ(S)) = φ(S). Lipschitz images satisfy H^m(h(A)) ≤ K^m·H^m(A) (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, which is in Submission's import closure). Hence H^m(φ(S)) ≤ K^m·H^m(ψ(S)).

5. (One radius per injective L.) Let L be injective and q > 1. An injective linear map on a finite-dimensional space is antilipschitz, so there is K ≥ 0 with |x − y| ≤ K|Lx − Ly| for all x, y. By step 1 and G(L) > 0 there is ε > 0 such that ‖L' − L‖ < ε implies G(L') < qG(L) and G(L) < qG(L'). Choose δ > 0 with δ < ε, δK < 1, (1 + δK)^m < q and (1 − δK)^{−m} < q. Then:
 (a) if ‖L' − L‖ ≤ δ, then G(L') ≤ qG(L) and G(L) ≤ qG(L');
 (b) if t ⊆ ℝ^m, φ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and |φ(x) − φ(y) − L(x − y)| ≤ δ|x − y| for all x, y ∈ t, then |φ(x) − φ(y) − (Lx − Ly)| ≤ δK|Lx − Ly|. Hence |φ(x) − φ(y)| ≤ (1 + δK)|Lx − Ly| and |Lx − Ly| ≤ (1 − δK)^{−1}|φ(x) − φ(y)|; in particular φ is injective on t. By steps 3 and 4, H^m(φ(t)) ≤ (1 + δK)^m·G(L)·L^m(t) ≤ q·G(L)·L^m(t), and G(L)·L^m(t) = H^m(L(t)) ≤ (1 − δK)^{−m}·H^m(φ(t)) ≤ q·H^m(φ(t)).

6. (Derivative control on an approximation piece.) Let t ⊆ ℝ^m be Borel, A linear, δ ≥ 0, and suppose |f(x) − f(y) − A(x − y)| ≤ δ|x − y| for x, y ∈ t and that Df(x) is a derivative of f within t at every x ∈ t. Then ‖Df(x) − A‖ ≤ δ for L^m-a.e. x ∈ t. Proof: almost every point of t is a Lebesgue density point of t (Besicovitch density theorem). Fix such a point x ∈ t, a vector z and ε > 0. For all small r > 0 the set t ∩ (x + r·closedBall(z, ε)) is nonempty, and |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε|y − x| for y ∈ t near x. Pick such an r and y = x + ra ∈ t with |a − z| ≤ ε. Then r|(Df(x) − A)a| ≤ |f(y) − f(x) − A(y − x)| + |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| ≤ (δ + ε)·r|a|, so |(Df(x) − A)z| ≤ |(Df(x) − A)a| + ‖Df(x) − A‖·|z − a| ≤ (δ + ε)(|z| + ε) + ‖Df(x) − A‖·ε. Letting ε → 0 gives |(Df(x) − A)z| ≤ δ|z|. This is the argument of Mathlib's ApproximatesLinearOn.norm_fderiv_sub_le, which does not use that the codomain is ℝ^m.

7. (Unweighted formula.) Let B ⊆ s be Borel. We show H^m(f(B)) = ∫_B J_f dL^m. If B = ∅ both sides vanish. Otherwise fix q > 1, and for each linear L let δ(L) > 0 be the radius of step 5 if L is injective and δ(L) := 1 otherwise. Since f is differentiable at each x ∈ B, Df(x) is a derivative of f within B at x. Mathlib's exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_n (n ∈ ℕ) with B ⊆ ⋃_n t_n, and linear maps A_n, such that |f(x) − f(y) − A_n(x − y)| ≤ δ(A_n)|x − y| on B_n := B ∩ t_n and A_n = Df(y_n) for some y_n ∈ B ⊆ s; so A_n is injective. By step 5(b), H^m(f(B_n)) ≤ q·G(A_n)·L^m(B_n) and G(A_n)·L^m(B_n) ≤ q·H^m(f(B_n)). By steps 6 and 5(a), G(Df(x)) ≤ q·G(A_n) and G(A_n) ≤ q·G(Df(x)) for a.e. x ∈ B_n; integrating, ∫_{B_n} J_f ≤ q·G(A_n)·L^m(B_n) and G(A_n)·L^m(B_n) ≤ q·∫_{B_n} J_f. Hence H^m(f(B_n)) ≤ q²∫_{B_n} J_f and ∫_{B_n} J_f ≤ q²·H^m(f(B_n)). The sets f(B_n) are Borel, because f is continuous and injective on the Borel set B_n (Lusin–Souslin; MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), and pairwise disjoint because f is injective on s. Summing over n by countable additivity of H^m and of B' ↦ ∫_{B'} J_f gives H^m(f(B)) ≤ q²∫_B J_f and ∫_B J_f ≤ q²·H^m(f(B)). Since q > 1 is arbitrary, letting q ↓ 1 gives H^m(f(B)) = ∫_B J_f dL^m.

8. (Proof of (ii).) f is continuous and injective on the Borel set s, so its restriction f_s : s → ℝ^P to the subtype s is a measurable embedding (Lusin–Souslin; ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding), and f(s) is Borel. Let ν be the measure on s with density ofReal(J_f) with respect to the restriction of L^m to s. For Borel C ⊆ ℝ^P the set B := s ∩ f⁻¹(C) = f_s⁻¹(C) (viewed in ℝ^m) is a Borel subset of s with f(B) = f(s) ∩ C, so by step 7, ν(f_s⁻¹(C)) = ∫_B J_f dL^m = H^m(f(s) ∩ C). Thus the push-forward of ν under f_s is H^m restricted to f(s). For a measurable embedding, ∫ g d((f_s)_*ν) = ∫ g∘f_s dν holds for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], without any measurability of g (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map). Unwinding the subtype (lintegral_subtype_comap) and the density (J_f is measurable by (i)) gives ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_s ofReal(J_f(x))·g(f(x)) dL^m(x). ∎
(Reused accepted declaration; its frozen type is byte-identical to the accepted node's. It is kernel-checked under the frozen imports, with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only, in candidate d5ba41d68f1c.)
proof_key_steps: G(L) := √det[⟨Le_k, Le_l⟩] is continuous, so J_f = G∘Df is Borel (measurable_fderiv): conclusion (i).
Linear area formula: for injective L = ι∘B (ι isometric, B invertible), G(L) = |det B| > 0 and H^m(L(S)) = G(L)·L^m(S).
Lipschitz comparison and continuity of G give, for each injective L and q > 1, a radius δ with q-comparisons for δ-approximations of L and for nearby linear maps.
Partition B ⊆ s into Borel pieces on which f is a δ(A_n)-approximation of an injective A_n = Df(y_n); density points give ‖Df − A_n‖ ≤ δ(A_n) a.e. on each piece.
Summing the per-piece q²-comparisons over the disjoint Borel images and letting q ↓ 1 gives H^m(f(B)) = ∫_B J_f for Borel B ⊆ s.
Pushing J_f·L^m on s forward along the measurable embedding f|_s gives H^m restricted to f(s), hence the weighted formula for every g: conclusion (ii).

subproblems.title: Gram-determinant chain rule along an orthonormal frame of range Λ, and positivity for injective Λ (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let m, d, P ∈ ℕ, let Λ : ℝ^m → ℝ^d be a (continuous) linear map and let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 (k < m) be the standard basis of ℝ^m. (i) If Λ is injective, then det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩]_{k,l} > 0. (ii) For every linear Γ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P and every orthonormal family σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{m−1}) in ℝ^d whose span equals range Λ, det[⟨ΓΛe_k, ΓΛe_l⟩]_{k,l} = det[⟨Γσ_i, Γσ_j⟩]_{i,j} · det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩]_{k,l}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m d P : ℕ) (Λ : Euclid m →L[ℝ] Euclid d), (Injective Λ → 0 < Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single l 1)))) ∧ ∀ (Γ : Euclid d →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (σ : Fin m → Euclid d), Orthonormal ℝ σ → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = LinearMap.range (Λ : Euclid m →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid d) → Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (Γ (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single k 1))) (Γ (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single l 1)))) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin m => inner ℝ (Γ (σ i)) (Γ (σ j))) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single l 1)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of the selected node (Jacobian factorization J(B∘A) = J(A)·J(B∘ι_R), Simon Ch. 2, 4.11) in Gram-determinant form, together with the positivity J(A) > 0 for injective A used in (7.1). Notation: e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 (k < m) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^m; all matrices are real m × m matrices indexed by Fin m.

1. (Frame coefficients.) Let σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{m−1}) be orthonormal in ℝ^d with span{σ_a} = range Λ, and put R_{al} := ⟨σ_a, Λe_l⟩. Since Λe_l ∈ range Λ = span{σ_a}, there are coefficients c_a with Λe_l = Σ_a c_a σ_a (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). Pairing with σ_b and using ⟨σ_b, σ_a⟩ = δ_{ab} gives c_b = ⟨σ_b, Λe_l⟩ = R_{bl} (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). Hence Λe_l = Σ_a R_{al} σ_a.

2. (Transformation rule.) Let Q ∈ ℕ and let G : ℝ^d → ℝ^Q be linear. By step 1, linearity of G and bilinearity of the real inner product, ⟨GΛe_k, GΛe_l⟩ = Σ_a Σ_b R_{ak}⟨Gσ_a, Gσ_b⟩R_{bl} = (Rᵀ[⟨Gσ_a, Gσ_b⟩]R)_{kl}. So [⟨GΛe_k, GΛe_l⟩] = Rᵀ[⟨Gσ_a, Gσ_b⟩]R.

3. (G := id, Q := d.) Orthonormality gives [⟨σ_a, σ_b⟩] = I. By step 2, [⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩] = RᵀR, so det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩] = det(Rᵀ)·det(R) = (det R)².

4. (Proof of (ii).) Let Γ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be linear and σ as in step 1. Step 2 with G := Γ, Q := P and multiplicativity of the determinant give det[⟨ΓΛe_k, ΓΛe_l⟩] = det(Rᵀ)·det[⟨Γσ_i, Γσ_j⟩]·det(R) = det[⟨Γσ_i, Γσ_j⟩]·(det R)². By step 3 this equals det[⟨Γσ_i, Γσ_j⟩]·det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩].

5. (Proof of (i).) Assume Λ is injective. Then range Λ has dimension m (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), so it has an orthonormal basis (b_0, …, b_{m−1}) indexed by Fin m (stdOrthonormalBasis reindexed). The vectors σ_a := b_a ∈ ℝ^d are orthonormal and span range Λ, so steps 1 and 3 apply with a matrix R. If Rv = 0 for some v ∈ ℝ^m, then Λ(Σ_l v_l e_l) = Σ_l v_l Σ_a R_{al}σ_a = Σ_a (Rv)_a σ_a = 0, hence Σ_l v_l e_l = 0 by injectivity of Λ, i.e. v = 0. So R is invertible, det R ≠ 0, and det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩] = (det R)² > 0 by step 3. (For m = 0 the determinant of the empty matrix is 1 > 0.) ∎
(Reused accepted declaration; its frozen type is byte-identical to the accepted node's. It is kernel-checked under the frozen imports in candidate d596f85ab9a9.)
proof_key_steps: For an orthonormal frame σ of range Λ, expand Λe_l = Σ_a R_{al}σ_a with R_{al} = ⟨σ_a, Λe_l⟩.
For every linear G, [⟨GΛe_k, GΛe_l⟩] = Rᵀ[⟨Gσ_a, Gσ_b⟩]R.
G = id gives det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩] = (det R)²; G = Γ then gives conclusion (ii).
For injective Λ and σ an orthonormal basis of range Λ, R is invertible, so det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩] = (det R)² > 0: conclusion (i).

subproblems.title: Determinant of (B∘ι_T)*(B∘ι_T) on a subspace T equals the Gram determinant of B on an orthonormal frame of T
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let T be a linear subspace of ℝ^P with the inner product of ℝ^P, let B : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be a continuous linear map, and let σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{k−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P with span{σ_0, …, σ_{k−1}} = T. Let ι_T : T → ℝ^P be the inclusion (T.subtypeL) and let * denote the adjoint for the inner products of T and ℝ^P. Then the determinant of the endomorphism (B∘ι_T)*(B∘ι_T) of T equals det[⟨Bσ_i, Bσ_j⟩]_{i,j<k}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (B : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (σ : Fin k → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ σ → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = T → ((B.comp T.subtypeL).adjoint ∘L (B.comp T.subtypeL)).det = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin k => inner ℝ (B (σ i)) (B (σ j)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the Notation paragraph of the supplied proof of the selected node ('for every orthonormal basis s_1, …, s_k of S, det(L*L) = det(Ls_i·Ls_j)_{i,j}, a Gram determinant'), applied to S := T and L := B∘ι_T. It converts the adjoint form of the Jacobian J^MΦ in the frozen statement into a Gram determinant on an orthonormal frame. Write C := (B∘ι_T)*(B∘ι_T) : T → T.

1. (σ lies in T.) Each σ_i belongs to span{σ_0, …, σ_{k−1}} = T. Let b_i ∈ T be σ_i regarded as an element of T, so ι_T(b_i) = σ_i.

2. (b is orthonormal in T.) The inner product of T is the restriction of the inner product of ℝ^P (Submodule.innerProductSpace), so ⟨b_i, b_j⟩_T = ⟨σ_i, σ_j⟩ = δ_{ij}.

3. (b spans T.) ι_T is injective and maps span_T{b_0, …, b_{k−1}} onto span{σ_0, …, σ_{k−1}} = T = ι_T(T) (Submodule.map_span, Submodule.map_subtype_top). Hence span_T{b_i} = T. Together with step 2, b = (b_0, …, b_{k−1}) is an orthonormal basis of T (OrthonormalBasis.mk); in particular dim T = k.

4. (Determinant via a matrix.) C is a continuous linear endomorphism of T and its determinant is that of the underlying linear map. The determinant of a linear endomorphism equals the determinant of its matrix [C]_b in any basis b of T (LinearMap.det_toMatrix).

5. (Matrix entries.) For an orthonormal basis, the i-th coordinate of w ∈ T is ⟨b_i, w⟩_T (OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply). Hence ([C]_b)_{ij} = ⟨b_i, C b_j⟩_T. By the defining property of the adjoint (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right), ⟨b_i, (B∘ι_T)*((B∘ι_T)b_j)⟩_T = ⟨(B∘ι_T)b_i, (B∘ι_T)b_j⟩ = ⟨Bσ_i, Bσ_j⟩.

6. (Conclusion.) Hence [C]_b = [⟨Bσ_i, Bσ_j⟩]_{i,j<k} and det C = det[⟨Bσ_i, Bσ_j⟩]_{i,j<k}. (If k = 0 then T = {0} and both sides equal 1; the argument above covers this case.) ∎
proof_key_steps: The σ_i lie in T and, viewed in T, form an orthonormal family (the inner product of T is the restricted one).
They span T because the inclusion is injective and maps their span onto span{σ_i} = T; so they form an orthonormal basis b of T.
det C equals the determinant of its matrix in b, whose (i, j) entry is ⟨b_i, C b_j⟩_T.
By the adjoint identity, ⟨b_i, (Bι_T)*(Bι_T)b_j⟩_T = ⟨Bσ_i, Bσ_j⟩, so the matrix is the Gram matrix.

subproblems.title: Borel partition of a Borel subset of an embedded C¹ submanifold subordinate to countably many charts
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded C¹ submanifold of dimension m (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M), and let E ⊆ M be Borel. Then there are sequences (E_k)_{k∈ℕ} of subsets of ℝ^P, (V_k)_{k∈ℕ} of subsets of ℝ^m, (W_k)_{k∈ℕ} of subsets of ℝ^P and maps ψ_k : ℝ^m → ℝ^P (k ∈ ℕ) such that: every E_k is Borel; the E_k are pairwise disjoint; ⋃_k E_k = E; and for every k, V_k and W_k are open, ψ_k is C¹ on V_k and injective on V_k, ψ_k(V_k) = W_k ∩ M, V_k ∩ ψ_k⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W_k, Dψ_k(z) = fderiv ℝ ψ_k z is injective for every z ∈ V_k, and E_k ⊆ W_k ∩ M.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (M E : Set (Euclid P)), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M → MeasurableSet E → E ⊆ M → ∃ (Es : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Vs : ℕ → Set (Euclid m)) (Ws : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (ψs : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid P), (∀ k, MeasurableSet (Es k)) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (Es i) (Es j)) ∧ (⋃ k, Es k) = E ∧ ∀ k, IsOpen (Vs k) ∧ IsOpen (Ws k) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (ψs k) (Vs k) ∧ InjOn (ψs k) (Vs k) ∧ ψs k '' Vs k = Ws k ∩ M ∧ (∀ K ⊆ Ws k, IsCompact K → IsCompact (Vs k ∩ ψs k ⁻¹' K)) ∧ (∀ z ∈ Vs k, Injective (fderiv ℝ (ψs k) z)) ∧ Es k ⊆ Ws k ∩ M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of the selected node (countable chart cover {W_k} of M and the disjoint Borel pieces E_k := (E ∩ W_k) ∖ (W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_{k−1})), packaged with the chart data that its step 8 uses.

1. (Charts.) By IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M, for every y ∈ M choose V_y ⊆ ℝ^m, W_y ⊆ ℝ^P and ψ_y : ℝ^m → ℝ^P such that V_y and W_y are open, y ∈ W_y, ψ_y is C¹ on V_y, ψ_y is injective on V_y, ψ_y(V_y) = W_y ∩ M, V_y ∩ ψ_y⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W_y, and Dψ_y(z) is injective for every z ∈ V_y. (The definition states smoothness as ContDiffOn with the natural number 1 cast to the smoothness-order type; this is the same condition as C¹, since ((1 : ℕ) : WithTop ℕ∞) = 1.)

2. (Countable subcover.) The sets W_y (y ∈ M) are open and ℝ^P is second countable, so by the Lindelöf property there is a countable set S ⊆ M with ⋃_{y∈S} W_y = ⋃_{y∈M} W_y (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable). As y ∈ W_y for y ∈ M, we get M ⊆ ⋃_{y∈S} W_y.

3. (Case S = ∅.) Then M ⊆ ⋃_{y∈∅} W_y = ∅, so M = ∅ and E = ∅ because E ⊆ M. Put E_k := ∅, V_k := ∅, W_k := ∅ and ψ_k := 0 for all k. Then each E_k is Borel, the E_k are pairwise disjoint, ⋃_k E_k = ∅ = E, V_k and W_k are open, ψ_k is C¹ and injective on ∅, ψ_k(∅) = ∅ = ∅ ∩ M, for every compact K ⊆ ∅ the set V_k ∩ ψ_k⁻¹(K) = ∅ is compact, the derivative condition is vacuous, and E_k = ∅ ⊆ W_k ∩ M.

4. (Case S ≠ ∅: enumeration.) A nonempty countable set is the range of a sequence, so S = {y_0, y_1, y_2, …} for some sequence (y_k)_{k∈ℕ} (repetitions allowed; Set.Countable.exists_eq_range). Put V_k := V_{y_k}, W_k := W_{y_k}, ψ_k := ψ_{y_k}. Since y_k ∈ S ⊆ M, step 1 shows that each (V_k, W_k, ψ_k) satisfies all chart conditions of the conclusion. Moreover ⋃_k W_k = ⋃_{y∈S} W_y ⊇ M by step 2.

5. (Pieces.) Put A_k := E ∩ W_k, which is Borel since E is Borel and W_k is open, and E_k := A_k ∖ ⋃_{j<k} A_j (Mathlib disjointed A k). Each E_k is Borel, as a finite Boolean combination of Borel sets (MeasurableSet.disjointed). The E_k are pairwise disjoint: for j < k, E_j ⊆ A_j and E_k ∩ A_j = ∅ (disjoint_disjointed). Their union is ⋃_k A_k (iUnion_disjointed: a point of ⋃_k A_k lies in E_k for the least k with x ∈ A_k). Finally ⋃_k A_k = E ∩ ⋃_k W_k = E, because E ⊆ M ⊆ ⋃_k W_k by step 4.

6. (Pieces lie in their chart.) E_k ⊆ A_k = E ∩ W_k ⊆ W_k ∩ M, since E ⊆ M. Together with steps 4 and 5 this gives every conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose a chart (V_y, W_y, ψ_y) with y ∈ W_y for every y ∈ M.
Lindelöf (second countability of ℝ^P): countably many W_y, y ∈ S ⊆ M, already cover M.
If S = ∅ then M = E = ∅ and empty charts and pieces work; otherwise enumerate S = {y_k}.
E_k := disjointed(E ∩ W_{y_k}) are Borel, pairwise disjoint, have union E, and E_k ⊆ W_{y_k} ∩ M.

subproblems.title: Jacobian factorization in a chart: J(B∘Dψ(v)) = J(Dψ(v))·J(B∘ι_{T_{ψ(v)}M}) (Simon Ch. 2, 4.11; (7.1) of the supplied proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, M, W ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^m, ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, a continuous linear map B : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and v ∈ V. Assume (V, W, ψ) is a chart of M: V and W are open, ψ is C¹ on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) = fderiv ℝ ψ z is injective for every z ∈ V. Let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 (k < m), T := span(tangentSpace M (ψ(v))) with the inner product of ℝ^P, and ι_T : T → ℝ^P the inclusion. Then √det[⟨B(Dψ(v)e_k), B(Dψ(v)e_l)⟩]_{k,l<m} = √det[⟨Dψ(v)e_k, Dψ(v)e_l⟩]_{k,l<m} · √det((B∘ι_T)*(B∘ι_T)), where the last determinant is that of an endomorphism of T, * is the adjoint for the inner products of T and ℝ^P, and √ is Real.sqrt.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (M W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (B : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (v : Euclid m), IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ M → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → v ∈ V → Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (B (fderiv ℝ ψ v (EuclideanSpace.single k 1))) (B (fderiv ℝ ψ v (EuclideanSpace.single l 1))))) = Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ v (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (fderiv ℝ ψ v (EuclideanSpace.single l 1)))) * Real.sqrt (((B.comp (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M (ψ v))).subtypeL).adjoint ∘L (B.comp (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M (ψ v))).subtypeL)).det)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of the selected node (Jacobian factorization J(B∘A) = J(A)·J(B∘ι_R), Simon Ch. 2, 4.11), applied as in its (7.1) with A := Dψ(v), whose range is T_{ψ(v)} by its step 2 (chart_tangent_space). Here it is written with Gram determinants through the sibling lemmas gram_chain and subspace_gram. Notation: Λ := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v, T := span(tangentSpace M (ψ(v))), ι_T : T → ℝ^P the inclusion.

1. (Tangent space.) The hypotheses are those of chart_tangent_space with N := M, d := m and r := 1 (1 ≤ 1, and the chart hypothesis "ψ is C¹ on V" is its hypothesis ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V for r = 1). Hence tangentSpace M (ψ(v)) = range Λ.

2. (T = range Λ.) range Λ is the carrier of the linear subspace LinearMap.range Λ, and the span of a linear subspace is the subspace itself (Submodule.span_eq). Hence T = span(range Λ) = LinearMap.range Λ.

3. (Dimension.) Λ is injective (chart hypothesis at v ∈ V), so dim range Λ = dim ℝ^m = m (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).

4. (Orthonormal frame.) Let (b_0, …, b_{m−1}) be an orthonormal basis of the m-dimensional inner product space range Λ, indexed by Fin m (stdOrthonormalBasis reindexed via step 3), and put σ_i := b_i ∈ ℝ^P. The inclusion of range Λ into ℝ^P is a linear isometry, so σ is orthonormal in ℝ^P (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry). The span of {σ_i} is the image under the inclusion of span{b_i}, which is all of range Λ; so span{σ_i} = range Λ (Submodule.span_image, Submodule.map_subtype_top).

5. (Gram chain.) Apply gram_chain with m := m, d := P, P := P, Λ := Dψ(v), Γ := B and the frame σ of step 4. Part (i), Λ being injective, gives c := det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩] > 0. Part (ii) gives det[⟨BΛe_k, BΛe_l⟩] = det[⟨Bσ_i, Bσ_j⟩]·c.

6. (Adjoint form.) By steps 2 and 4, span{σ_i} = range Λ = T. subspace_gram with P := P, k := m, the subspace T, the map B and the frame σ gives a := det((B∘ι_T)*(B∘ι_T)) = det[⟨Bσ_i, Bσ_j⟩].

7. (Square roots.) By steps 5 and 6, det[⟨BΛe_k, BΛe_l⟩] = a·c with c > 0. For c ≥ 0 and every real a, √(a·c) = √a·√c (Real.sqrt_mul'; no sign condition on a is needed). Hence √det[⟨B(Λe_k), B(Λe_l)⟩] = √a·√c = √c·√a = √det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩]·√det((B∘ι_T)*(B∘ι_T)). ∎
proof_key_steps: chart_tangent_space (r = 1) gives tangentSpace M (ψ v) = range Dψ(v), so T = span(range Dψ(v)) = LinearMap.range Dψ(v).
Dψ(v) is injective, so range Dψ(v) is m-dimensional; an orthonormal basis of it gives an orthonormal frame σ : Fin m → ℝ^P spanning T.
gram_chain: det[⟨BΛe_k, BΛe_l⟩] = det[⟨Bσ_i, Bσ_j⟩]·det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩], the last factor positive.
subspace_gram: det[⟨Bσ_i, Bσ_j⟩] = det((B∘ι_T)*(B∘ι_T)).
Take square roots with Real.sqrt_mul' (positive factor c) and commute the product.

subproblems.title: Area formula for a C¹ map on a Borel subset of one chart of an embedded C¹ submanifold (Simon Ch. 2, 4.11–4.13; steps 4–8 of the supplied proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, M, E, W ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^m, ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and Φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Assume (V, W, ψ) is a chart of M: V and W are open, ψ is C¹ on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) is injective for every z ∈ V. Assume further that E is Borel with E ⊆ W ∩ M, that Φ is C¹ on ℝ^P, that Φ is injective on E, and that DΦ(x) = fderiv ℝ Φ x is injective for every x ∈ E. For x ∈ ℝ^P let T_x := span(tangentSpace M x) with the inner product of ℝ^P, ι_x : T_x → ℝ^P the inclusion and J^MΦ(x) := √det((DΦ(x)∘ι_x)*(DΦ(x)∘ι_x)) (* the adjoint for the inner products of T_x and ℝ^P, det of an endomorphism of T_x, √ = Real.sqrt). Then H^m(Φ(E)) = ∫⁻_E ENNReal.ofReal(J^MΦ(x)) dH^m(x) in [0, ∞], where H^m := μHE[m].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (M E W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (Φ : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ M → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → MeasurableSet E → E ⊆ W ∩ M → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → InjOn Φ E → (∀ x ∈ E, Injective (fderiv ℝ Φ x)) → μHE[m] (Φ '' E) = ∫⁻ x in E, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt ((((fderiv ℝ Φ x).comp (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x)).subtypeL).adjoint ∘L ((fderiv ℝ Φ x).comp (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x)).subtypeL)).det)) ∂μHE[m]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4, 5, 6 and 8 of the supplied proof of the selected node, for a single chart. Its step 5 cites SimonGMT injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative, which is not in Submission's import closure. The accepted sibling gram_area supplies both that Euclidean area formula ((5.1) and (5.2)) and the change of variables of step 6. Its weighted form holds for every weight g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] without measurability, so the Borel measurability of J^MΦ (step 7 of the supplied proof) is not needed. Notation: e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1; for f : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, J_f(v) := √det[⟨Df(v)e_k, Df(v)e_l⟩]_{k,l<m} (the Jacobian of gram_area); H^m := μHE[m]; L^m := volume on ℝ^m.

1. (The coordinate piece.) Let F := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(E) ⊆ ℝ^m. F is Borel. Indeed, the function ψ̃ equal to ψ on V and to 0 off V is Borel measurable, because ψ is continuous on the open (hence Borel) set V and the constant 0 is continuous on its complement (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise). Moreover F = V ∩ ψ̃⁻¹(E) with E Borel.

2. (Images.) ψ(F) = E. Clearly ψ(F) ⊆ E. Conversely, if x ∈ E then x ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), say x = ψ(v) with v ∈ V, and then v ∈ F. Hence also Φ(E) = Φ(ψ(F)) = (Φ∘ψ)(F).

3. (Differentiability and chain rule.) For v ∈ V, ψ is C¹ on the open set V, hence differentiable at v (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn, and V is a neighbourhood of v). Φ is C¹ on ℝ^P, hence differentiable everywhere (ContDiff.differentiable). By the chain rule, Φ∘ψ is differentiable at v and D(Φ∘ψ)(v) = DΦ(ψ(v))∘Dψ(v) (fderiv_comp).

4. (Hypotheses of gram_area on F.) Let v ∈ F. Dψ(v) is injective (chart hypothesis) and DΦ(ψ(v)) is injective (ψ(v) ∈ E), so D(Φ∘ψ)(v) = DΦ(ψ(v))∘Dψ(v) is injective. ψ is injective on F ⊆ V. Φ∘ψ is injective on F: if Φ(ψ(v)) = Φ(ψ(w)) with v, w ∈ F, then ψ(v) = ψ(w) because Φ is injective on E and ψ(v), ψ(w) ∈ E, and then v = w because ψ is injective on V.

5. (Area of Φ(E), (5.2).) gram_area (ii) with f := Φ∘ψ, s := F and g :≡ 1 gives H^m((Φ∘ψ)(F)) = ∫⁻_{(Φ∘ψ)(F)} 1 dH^m = ∫⁻_F ofReal(J_{Φ∘ψ}(v))·1 dL^m(v). By step 2 the left side is H^m(Φ(E)).

6. (Change of variables, step 6.) gram_area (ii) with f := ψ, s := F and the weight g(x) := ofReal(J^MΦ(x)) gives, using ψ(F) = E, ∫⁻_E ofReal(J^MΦ(x)) dH^m(x) = ∫⁻_F ofReal(J_ψ(v))·ofReal(J^MΦ(ψ(v))) dL^m(v).

7. (Pointwise identity (7.1).) Let v ∈ F. By step 3, D(Φ∘ψ)(v)e_k = DΦ(ψ(v))(Dψ(v)e_k) for every k. chart_jacobian, applied to the given chart, B := DΦ(ψ(v)) and v ∈ V, gives J_{Φ∘ψ}(v) = J_ψ(v)·J^MΦ(ψ(v)). Since J_ψ(v) ≥ 0, ofReal(J_ψ(v)·J^MΦ(ψ(v))) = ofReal(J_ψ(v))·ofReal(J^MΦ(ψ(v))) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul).

8. (Conclusion, step 8.) F is Borel, and by step 7 the integrands in steps 5 and 6 agree at every point of F, so the two integrals over F are equal (setLIntegral_congr_fun). Therefore H^m(Φ(E)) = ∫⁻_E ofReal(J^MΦ(x)) dH^m(x). This is the claim: J^MΦ(x) is exactly √det(((DΦ(x))∘ι_x)*((DΦ(x))∘ι_x)) with T_x = span(tangentSpace M x). ∎
proof_key_steps: F := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(E) is Borel, ψ(F) = E and (Φ∘ψ)(F) = Φ(E).
On F, ψ and Φ∘ψ are differentiable with injective derivatives D(Φ∘ψ) = DΦ(ψ)∘Dψ, and both maps are injective on F.
gram_area for Φ∘ψ with weight 1: H^m(Φ(E)) = ∫_F J_{Φ∘ψ} dL^m.
gram_area for ψ with weight ofReal∘J^MΦ (no measurability needed): ∫_E J^MΦ dH^m = ∫_F J_ψ·(J^MΦ∘ψ) dL^m.
chart_jacobian with B = DΦ(ψ(v)) gives J_{Φ∘ψ} = J_ψ·(J^MΦ∘ψ) on F, so the two integrals over F agree.
